b1problems:
1. BLOCKING: edges are clipped off the canvas. Q10 was done as SVG padding only: SVG_MARGIN is 16 (src/scene.rs:45, used at to_svg ~4775) while the scene keeps its 28 px MARGIN gutter. The router may route in that gutter: src/router.rs:125 `ROUTE_OUTER = MARGIN / 2`, commented 'so a detour round the outermost node stays on the canvas'. grow_scene (src/scene.rs:5181) adds only e.bezier and curve_geometry for an edge, never its waypoint spline or route. Routes up to about 28 px beyond the drawing used to fit inside the 28 px padding; with 16 they now fall off the canvas.

Corpus evidence: advanced.mmd in route() mode (quality --svg advanced.routed.svg). The vertical leg of Scan → Dev 'fail' sits at x=723.0 in a 721-wide viewBox, so the whole 2 px stroke is outside; before the package it was at 735.0 in 745. The rendered PNG shows the dashed edge leaving the canvas on the right and coming back.

Extra inputs: in ex3/x3_long.mmd (static) the start → a1 leg is at x=-11.8 in a 292-wide viewBox, only two stubs are visible, and the vertical run is gone; before it was at 0.2. In 60 random flowcharts (verify/b1-arrows/rnd) the package newly clips r56 (n7 → n11 at x=950.7, viewBox width 938; before 962.7 in 962) and r22 (2.8 px). It makes r01 and r31 12 px worse (17.9 -> 29.9 and 20.5 -> 32.5 px past the canvas).

Suggested fix: grow the SVG canvas over the drawn curve, e.g. edge_polyline or the painted segments plus half the stroke, in grow_scene or at least in to_svg. Alternatively keep the painted padding at least as wide as the gutter the router can use. Add a quality gate for strokes outside the viewBox.

2. NON-BLOCKING: M1's 'last head length straight' still fails for about a third of glyph ends. end_kink on the perf corpus is 85/257 static and 101/257 routed; the gate fixtures give 60|77. A square head on a turning S-cubic shows an elbow or hook at the head base. Example: advanced Gate → Job Queue (thick) paints `... 186.7 184.8 C 185.4 186.5, 182.1 187.1, 182.1 189.2 L 182.1 192.0`, a 5 px hook that is visible at 2.5x zoom. In fanout-frames n0 → g1 the stroke arrives nearly vertical into a head pointing right (an L-shape). The implementer documents this as needing a different edge shape.

3. NON-BLOCKING: routed end_tilt barely moved (25 -> 24 on the perf corpus). Sixteen bench-75 routed ends still face 73-128 deg off the side normal (job1->ext and dash->ext 128.4 deg, svc4->metrics 116.6 deg), unchanged from before the package; they are ports-stage ends turned round a corner. The 95% criterion holds only barely in routed mode (95.1%).

4. NON-BLOCKING: a very wide linkStyle stroke ends badly. ex3/x1_styles.mmd, `linkStyle 2 stroke-width:14px`, paints `... C 139.6 220.4, 142.0 221.6, 144.4 222.6 L 145.9 222.6` with marker arrow-t11__3a3 (refX 0). The 14 px butt end is wider than the 11 px head and has a notched corner where the slanted curve meets the 1.5 px level run (verify/b1-arrows/z3/x1_green.png).

5. NON-BLOCKING (drag-only, degenerate): when a curve is shorter than trim + 1 px (nodes about 4-6 px apart mid-drag), the stroke is drawn whole and the refX 5 head reaches 5.5 px past the curve's end into the target node. Picking does not cover that ink. Example: fanout drag scene, e2 A->B3, bezier (460.85,126) -> (464.95,126.23); the painted head tip lands at about (470.4,126.4).

6. NON-BLOCKING: to_svg is slower on large synthetic graphs (render_svg syn400 93 -> 131 ms, syn1000 195 -> 287 ms), because the painter squares each turning end. This is within the 2x static budget.
b1unfixed:
- Q10 MARGIN 16 in scene coordinates (layout.rs): done only as the SVG padding (SVG_MARGIN) while the scene and router keep the 28 px gutter. The reason for the skip (float-exact router tie-breaks would move routes) is plausible. As built, though, the skip is NOT legitimate yet: it clips routed edges (see the blocking problem). Either the canvas must cover the drawn routes, or the router's outer room must fit within SVG_MARGIN.
- M1: router end stub >= 2*ARROW_MARKER_PX + corner radius (router.rs, ROUTE_CLEAR + STUB_EXTRA): skipped. Lengthening the stub in the search moved dense-fixture routes (+12-40% overlap/tight); the attempt is kept as b1/router_longstub.patch. Given the 'no other layout change' constraint and the later routing packages, the skip is legitimate.
- M1: last head length straight for strongly turning single cubics, done in the scene: skipped. The painter squares an end only within about 1 px of the scene curve, and falls back to entering along the tangent line; end_kink 60|77 remain. The case that a cubic cannot do it (handles capped at half the border gap) is credible; it belongs to the orthogonal or edge-shape work (report §2.1). Legitimate, but the visible elbows remain.
- Report §2.4 ports-stage spreading of ends on over-full sides: out of B1's scope. The painter-side narrowing (arrow-w markers) is an acceptable interim.
